v1.feedback: The Physarum simulation is a solid choice — slime mold networks produce genuinely recognizable organic form, and the zigzag lattice-snap is a clever interpretation of the brief that actually shows up in the motion (angle quantization to 45° during the crystallization phase). The warm amber-to-cool blue palette shift during zigzag events is restrained and reads well against the dark ground. Two things to tighten: the trail plane overlay at 0.4 opacity muddies the particle structure — drop it to 0.15 or render trails as a second point pass so the network edges stay crisp. Also the orthographic camera clips the colony once it spreads past ~30 units; add a slow dolly-out or fit-to-bounds so the full network stays framed as it grows, avoiding the tiny-subject-in-vast-canvas trap late in the simulation.

v2.feedback: The zigzag concept lands — the periodic snap-to-45° lattice crystallization is a genuine formal swerve, not just a palette swap, and the warm-to-cool color shift reinforces the organic→crystalline transition. However, the 80k particles spread across 3-5 random source clusters risk reading as disconnected blobs during the organic phase; consolidating to 1-2 sources or adding inter-cluster chemotactic bridges would give a stronger silhouette. The trail point-cloud at 512×512 is expensive for how faint it renders (alpha 0.12 × intensity) — either pump trail visibility so the network structure is readable in 2s, or drop it and save the draw call. The zigzag hold time (2.5s) is too brief to appreciate the lattice snap; stretch it to 4-5s so the crystalline geometry has time to propagate visibly before melting back.
